mentions.name: CodeHydra
mentions.description: A multi-workspace IDE for parallel AI agent development. It points at one or more local or remote git repos and creates lightweight workspaces via git worktrees, each with its own embedded VS Code and AI agent (supports Claude Code and OpenCode). A sidebar shows real-time status indicators for which agents are idle or busy, and strong keyboard navigation covers creating, deleting, and switching workspaces. Agents can also control CodeHydra itself through an MCP server—closing their workspace when done, spawning new workspaces for sub-tasks with an initial prompt, or automating VS Code (e.g., opening a browser preview tab or files). Built with Electron + Svelte 5 + TypeScript, MIT licensed, runs on Linux/macOS/Windows, and starts via npx or uvx.
mentions.problem: The author lacked a good tool to orchestrate multiple AI coding agents: waiting for one agent to finish before starting the next, juggling multiple terminals to see which agents were busy or idle, agents clashing when run against the same repo, and friction from manually creating git worktrees.
